micronarrative: The bakery celebrating a religious holiday stood out to me. I felt uncomfortable when I read how it was shown as erasing traditional culture and promoting dangerous ideologies. I have never encountered such a thing personally since I live in New York and there is a diverse culture over here, but I have felt uncomfortable when I first moved here because I was given stares when I wore hijab. In the beginning, I felt I needed to fit in to avoid the uncomfortable feeling, but later on people got better. I never changed how I speak. It was usually how I dressed up, nothing else. This experience of adjusting my appearance to navigate public spaces connects to the scenario’s tension between individual expression and community backlash. While the bakery faced organized hostility, my own discomfort stemmed from subtle social pressure to conform visually, highlighting how visibility can invite both scrutiny and the need for self-preservation in diverse settings.
